bibl.title: The Best of the Grammarians. Aristarchus of Samothrace on the Iliad.
bibl.seg: Francesca Schironi, The Best of the Grammarians. Aristarchus of Samothrace on the Iliad.
Ann Arbor, University of Michigan Press, 2018, xxvi-908 pp. ISBN 978-0-472-13076-4. $150.
C.R. par Richard Hunter, JHS 139 (2019) pp. 283-284.
bibl.note: Preface. - Part 1. Aristarchus: Contexts and Sources: 1.1. Aristarchus: life, sources, and selection of fragments; - 1.2. Aristarchus on Homer: monographs, editions, and commentaries. - Part 2. Aristarchus at Work: 2.1. Critical signs: the bridge between edition and commentary; - 2.2. Aristarchus and manuscript evidence; - 2.3. Paraphrase: a ubiquitous interpretative tool. - Part 3. The Six Parts of Grammar: 3.0. The six parts of grammar; - 3.1. Reading aloud: the interpretative effort of reading; - 3.2.A. Interpretation of poetic tropes: decoding Homer's style and figurative language; - 3.2.B. Interpretation of poetic figures: decoding Homer's syntax; - 3.3.A. Explanation of glossai: diving into the microcosm of Homeric vocabulary; - 3.3.B. Explanation of historiai: characters, customs, and places of the heroic world; - 3.4. Discovery of etymology: an objective, multipurpose practice; - 3.5. Calculation of analogy: a "scientific" method applied to the text; - 3.6.A. Judgment of poems: Aristotle's lesson; - 3.6.B. Judgment of poems: the "art" of athetesis; - 3.6.C. Judgment of poems: the art of "saving" the Homeric text. - Part 4. Aristarchus and his colleagues: 1. Aristarchus and Zenodotus; - 2. Aristarchus and Aristophanes of Byzantium; - 3. Aristarchus and other Alexandrian scholars; - 4. Aristarchus and Crates of Mallos; - 5. Conclusions. - Part 5. Aristarchus' Homer: 5.1. Aristarchus and Homeric language; - 5.2. The "Homeric Question"; - 5.3. Homer and the Neoteroi; - 5.4. Aristarchus and Homeric characters. - 6. Conclusions. - Technical terms often used in this book. Bibliography. Indexes.
